lesson.title: Corner Frequency: Same Number, Different Picture
lesson.summary: Corner frequency names the same value as cutoff frequency but describes its role as the point where the straight line asymptotes of a log log magnitude plot meet.
lesson.body:
Corner frequency and cutoff frequency refer to the same numeric value for a simple first order filter, but they describe two different things. Cutoff frequency, from the previous chapter, is a property of the actual, curved frequency response: it is where the real magnitude crosses the half power point. Corner frequency is a property of a simplified sketch of that response, the straight line, or asymptotic, version of the Bode magnitude plot. It is the frequency at which two straight line segments, drawn to approximate the curve, meet and change slope.

For the resistor capacitor low pass filter from the cutoff frequency chapter, with R equal to 1000 ohms and C equal to 0.1 microfarads, the cutoff frequency was computed as f_c equals 1591.5 Hz, where omega_c equals 1 over RC equals 10,000 rad/s. On the actual curve, the magnitude there is 0.7071 of maximum, or negative 3.01 dB. On the straight line sketch, the flat 0 dB line running below the corner and the sloped negative 20 dB per decade line running above the corner both pass through exactly 0 dB at omega equals 10,000 rad/s, since that is where the two lines are defined to intersect.

That gap, 3.01 dB, between the idealized corner at 0 dB and the real curve at negative 3.01 dB, is not a mistake or a rounding error. It is the built in inaccuracy of using two straight lines to approximate a smooth curve, and it is largest exactly at the corner. The name corner frequency is really a warning label: it tells you this is the one frequency where the straight line approximation is at its least accurate, even though the frequency value itself is exact. The next few chapters build on this same corner point to define the edges of a passband and a stopband, and the asymptotic approximation chapter later in this unit returns to quantify exactly how the error shrinks as you move away from the corner.
